title: BitMoD: Bit-serial Mixture-of-Datatype LLM Acceleration
problem: LLM deployment is constrained by large weight memory footprints; existing low-precision quantization schemes either sacrifice too much accuracy or lack hardware support for multiple heterogeneous data types simultaneously. Current accelerators cannot efficiently process mixed numerical formats (e.g., INT4, FP4, NF4) within a single design.
motivation: Memory bandwidth and capacity are the primary bottleneck for LLM inference, and sub-4-bit quantization is necessary to fit large models on edge/server hardware without unacceptable accuracy degradation.
method: BitMoD divides neural network weights into small groups (128 weights each) and selects the best numerical compression format for each group—choosing from formats like INT4, FP4, or NF4—to minimize information loss. The hardware uses a bit-serial processing design (processing one bit at a time), which naturally handles all these different formats by converting them internally to a unified representation; a specialized unit then rescales each group's results with minimal overhead.
key_novelty: The core insight is that per-group numerical-format assignment becomes practical when paired with bit-serial hardware that processes all formats through a unified internal representation, eliminating the need for separate processing circuits per format.
contributions: Fine-grained data-type adaptation that assigns a distinct numerical type to each 128-weight group to preserve accuracy at 3-4 bit precision
Bit-serial processing element with a unified internal representation supporting heterogeneous weight types without datapath duplication
Bit-serial dequantization unit that rescales per-group partial sums with minimal area overhead
Demonstrated 1.69x and 1.48x speedup over ANT and OliVe accelerators with <0.5% accuracy loss at 4-bit and better perplexity than prior art at 3-bit

metrics.accuracy: <0.5% accuracy loss at 4-bit (discriminative); better perplexity than prior at 3-bit (generative)

limitations: Evaluation targets weight-only quantization; activation quantization and KV-cache compression are not addressed.
primary_theme: mixed-datatype bit-serial LLM weight quantization accelerator
